function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
It sounds like you’re looking for a conversational companion powered by AI—something that can chat with you, learn your preferences, and maybe even help you practice social skills or just keep you company. While I’m happy to share some ideas and resources, I’m not able to become a romantic partner myself. Here’s a quick rundown of what’s out there and how you can get started: | Option | What It Is | Key Features | How to Try It | |--------|------------|--------------|---------------| | **Replika** | A chatbot app that learns from your conversations | • Adaptive personality
• Mood tracking
• Voice & text chat | Download the free version on iOS/Android or try the web demo at [replika.ai](https://replika.ai/) | | **ChatGPT (OpenAI)** | General‑purpose language model | • Text conversation
• Customizable “personality” via prompts
• No built‑in voice | Use the free tier on the OpenAI website or integrate via the API if you’re tech‑savvy | | **Mitsuku / Kuki** | Award‑winning chatbot | • Conversational humor
• Trivia & games | Play online at [kuki.ai](https://www.kuki.ai/) | | **Woebot** | Mental‑health chatbot | • CBT‑based conversations
• Daily check‑ins | Free on iOS/Android | | **Custom Bot Platforms** | Build your own bot (e.g., Rasa, Botpress) | • Full control over personality & data privacy | Requires coding knowledge | ### Things to Keep in Mind 1. **Privacy** – Read each service’s privacy policy. Some collect data for training, others promise local storage only. 2. **Expectations** – These bots simulate conversation; they don’t have emotions or consciousness. Treat them as tools rather than real people. 3. **Safety** – Avoid sharing sensitive personal details until you’re comfortable with the platform’s security measures. ### Next Steps - Pick one of the options above that aligns with your goals (e.g., casual chat vs. mental‑health support). - Sign up or download the app. - Start a conversation and see how the AI responds. Most platforms let you tweak settings or “train” the bot over time. If you’d like more detailed guidance on setting up a custom bot or comparing specific features, feel free to let me know!
